project_metadata.job_description: Seeking a skilled CAD design engineer to convert measured parts from photos into STEP or Inventor 3D files, including manufacturing drawings. The ideal candidate will have experience in precision engineering and be able to accurately translate 2D measurements into 3D models. Attention to detail and the ability to deliver high-quality designs are essential.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Yes, certainly. In fact, I complete most of my projects this way, using photos with the dimensions marked on them.
I am also very interested in long-term cooperation.
Best regards,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:

Provided that this suits you, I would rather handle the first project at a fixed price.

The countersinks also seem designed to accommodate the heads of countersunk screws, but that would suggest that the bushing is fitted from the other side. Could you clarify the actual assembly method?
The photos also clearly omit some parts belonging to the complete shaft assembly. As a result, I still cannot fully understand the mechanism's operating principle.

Attached is the first fully completed version of the drawings. Because I still have not received details explaining how the bushing is to be fitted and retained, please disregard its present design. For now, the drawing simply shows it fastened by three screws.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Good afternoon, [CLIENT_NAME_001]. Has everything been clear up to this point? Are there any comments, changes, or further requests from your side? When can I anticipate your feedback?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Hi, I am reviewing it at the moment. Hopefully, I will get back to you today with all the necessary clarification. [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for being patient.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_002],
I have finally managed to inspect everything and review the drawings you provided.

1\. The main difference, which I had not realized before, is that we must produce premachined parts, weld them together, and carry out the final machining afterward. This applies to POS 1+2+3.

2\. The raw input material for the main shaft is tube 108/28, which will be premachined to provide the locations for POS 2+3.

3\. The previously unclear bushing is installed inside the main shaft. **IMPORTANT**: my notes state this incorrectly—the bushing is not fitted to POS 4 and belongs only in the main shaft. Please select an appropriate clearance between the bushing and shaft.

4\. POS 4 carries the piston/rod end together with the nut. The rod from the control piston, which provides the sliding movement, runs inside the main shaft. This is why the inner dia of 55mm must also be machined following welding.

5\. Cross section C-C on the mainshaft drw. shows that this keyway is to be omitted. Instead, the thread for the M100x2 locking nut needs to be wider, and the space for the main bushing must also be wider (40mm).

6\. Where possible, please number the drawings according to the numbering shown on the assembly.

Please update me on the progress, and [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The bushing configuration now makes sense. There is still one question, though: are you certain its length is correct? Relative to the machined seat within the shaft, the bushing appears quite short.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Just to confirm, should these lugs lie in the same plane? They look offset in the photos, so I thought the offset was intentional.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: No. As stated in the message (it is shown incorrectly in the drawings), the bushing sits inside the main shaft, and the rod from the control piston is guided through this bushing. Therefore, you need to select a suitable clearance, such as H8/h9, between the bushing and the inner diameter of the shaft. The sliding part contains only the end of the piston.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The angle between the hole axes is 45 degrees, matching both the picture and your assembly.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I think I may be misunderstanding this again. If the bushing is installed only inside the main shaft, does that mean it no longer has to be secured by screws?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: With a clearance fit, wouldn’t the bushing remain loose and move inside the shaft? Or is it rigidly mounted on the piston rod?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Since face 1 is flat, I do not believe it needs a machining allowance. Once welded, this face could not be machined on a lathe and still remain flat. We could, however, add a machining allowance to face 2. Another option would be to leave an allowance on face 1 too, then mill it flat after welding. What is your opinion?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I was informed that this bushing is located only in the shaft. However, I am considering another possible arrangement: the bushing would also be secured at the sliding end with the rod nut through it, while the bushing itself would slide inside the main shaft, using its outside diameter as the contact surface. Please prepare it this way. After the drawings are finalized, I will show them to the maintanence manager, and perhaps he will suggest another idea. For now, please proceed like this.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: At this point, should the holes be deleted from the bushing, or should they remain in both the bushing and the sliding mandrel?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
You are correct: surface 1 should not be machined after welding.
The same applies to surface 2, because machining it would be very difficult. Both surfaces therefore need to be finished before they are welded onto the shaft. Is that acceptable?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Please leave them unchanged.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: ок

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: That is a good question. I believe there should still be a small groove separating the thread from the bearing surface, though it could perhaps be smaller.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Okay, I’ll prepare the second version and send it for approval either later tonight or tomorrow.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Perfect, [FREELANCER_NAME_003] you

messages.speaker: freelancer

Good evening,
I’ve reviewed the drawings. Honestly, the version without colours is easier to read. The 3D views could perhaps remain coloured, but every other view should be without colours.
Only very minor corrections are needed; please refer to the notes added to the drawings.

Once this project is finalized, could you provide dwg/dxf files in addition to the pdf files, if possible?

[FREELANCER_NAME_003] you for making the updates.

messages.text:

For the 3D models, I will provide STEP files together with the original editable SolidWorks formats: SLDPRT, SLDASM and SLDDRW. Besides STEP, I can also export the models in SAT, IGES or IFC formats.

First, please send the final drawing set in pdf. I will confirm it, and you can then export the other formats.
For the required formats: PDF+DWG and STEP+ editable solidworks 3D files and drawings.

[FREELANCER_NAME_003] you.
